name: Turka
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Hurlimann, Ruth & Eunice V. Pike. 1985. A note on tone and stress in Cerman. JWAL 15(2): 56-60. [sister language Cerma, NOT Turka]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For Cerma (not Turka): 'For the most part, stress occurs on the next to the last syllable of a word, but because it does not always occur in that environment, there is contrastive placement of stress.' Cited here only as closest-relative context.

sources.citation: Prost, Andre. 1964. Le tyurama. In: Contribution a l'etude des langues voltaiques (Memoires de l'IFAN 70), 75-120. Dakar: IFAN. [Rosetta Project excerpts: intro p. 75; Chapitre I Phonetique pp. 77-79; Textes]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.42.105.28.7.65 (70)); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.42.105.28.7.65 (70)
sources.note: The Phonetique chapter (vowels, consonants, consonant clusters, word structure CV/CCV/CVC/CVC'V'/CVC'C''V') has no section on tone or accent and never uses the word 'accent'. (The sister Kirma chapter in the same volume speaks of 'voyelle breve accentuee' conditioning suffix-consonant gemination but states no placement rule; the Tyurama chapter's primes in CVC'V' are segment indices, not accent marks -- verified on a 300 dpi render.) Remaining pp. 80-120 (morphology/syntax) not in the excerpt.

sources.citation: Suggett, Colin. 2006 [1st ed. 2003]. En avant pour le tchourama! Guide d'orthographe tchourama. 2e ed. Ouagadougou: SIL. 96 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 30702/30704; subject 'Phonological descriptions; Orthography')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Ch. 4 'Les tons' (p. 31ff): words are composed of 'les voyelles, les consonnes et les tons'; accents graves/aigus in the orthography mark tone melodies (six written melodies), not vowel quality or stress.

sources.citation: Suggett, Colin J. 2005 [1999]. Tone in tchourama (Turka): A Descriptive Summary. Submitted to TSD November 1999, revised July 2005. Ouagadougou: SIL Burkina Faso. ii+25 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Chapters: consonants, vowels, phonotactics (syllable types CV, N, V, CVV, CCV, CCVV, CVC, CVVC; word-structure statistics), contrasts, orthography proposal. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur; tone is deferred to the companion tone paper ('The vast majority of base verb forms are underlying toneless and consequently their pitch depends entirely on the preceding subject pronoun').

sources.citation: Suggett, Colin & Dot Suggett (compilers). 2003. Lexique tchourama-francais, francais-tchourama. Edition preliminaire. Ouagadougou: SIL. 141 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Front matter (pp. 1-20 read) refers the reader to the Guide d'orthographe for spelling/tone conventions; no stress information.

sources.citation: Berthelette, John. 2002 [survey 1995/2001]. Sociolinguistic survey report for the Tyurama (Turka) language. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-008. Dallas: SIL International. 47 pp.
